title: 6.11.7 Lab: Music for every screen
description: Star catch has a title, the game, a win and a loss, and every change of screen goes through goTo(next). Make goTo change the music: stop what was playing, loop the tune on the title and in the game, and play it once for a win or a loss.

steps.title: Stop the music first
steps.instructions:
The starter is Star catch with screens, using the state variable of 6.6.7: `state` is `'title'`, `'play'`, `'won'` or `'lost'`. Enter on the title starts a game; 10 catches win; 3 misses lose; R on an end screen goes back to the title. Every change of screen goes through one function, `goTo(next)`, and so far it only does `state = next;`. `setup()` loads one tune, `music`, and ends with `goTo('title')`. Run it and play a game to the end: no music anywhere. That is this lab.

Music changes when the screen changes, so it belongs in `goTo`, not in `draw()` (6.11.6). First, at the top of `goTo`, stop whatever is playing with `music.stop();`. Without it two things go wrong: `loop()` while the tune is already looping does nothing, and `play()` starts a second copy on top of the first.
hints: `music.stop();` is the first line inside `goTo(next)`, above `state = next;`.

steps.title: The title and the game loop the tune
hints: `next` is the screen being entered; `state = next;` has just set `state` to it.
Click the canvas before you press Enter: the click switches sound on and gives the sketch your keys (5.1.13).

steps.title: A win and a loss play it once
steps.instructions: A win and a loss each play the tune once, not looping, so the end screen goes quiet after it. Add two more `if`s in `goTo`: for `'won'`, `music.rate = 1.25;` (faster and higher), then `music.play();`; for `'lost'`, `music.rate = 0.6;` (slow and low), then `music.play();`. Play to a win and to a loss, and press R after each: the title's tune comes back, alone, because `goTo('title')` stopped the end tune first.
hints: `play()`, not `loop()`: the end tune plays once and then stops by itself.
To reach a win sooner while you test, change the `10` in `if (score >= 10)` to `2`, then put it back.

requirements.title: A new screen stops the old music
requirements.description: Inside goTo(next), a sound's .stop() runs, so the last screen's music cannot carry on under the next one. Help: 6.11.6 (Reading: Music that follows the game)
requirements.hint: music.stop(); as the first line of goTo(next).

requirements.title: The title and the game loop the tune
requirements.description: Inside goTo(next), .loop() runs under an if (or a case) on the screen being entered: one for the title and one for the game, or one if that asks for both. Help: 6.11.6 (Reading: Music that follows the game)
requirements.hint: if (next === 'title') { music.rate = 0.8; music.loop(); }, and the same for 'play' with rate 1.

requirements.title: A win and a loss play it once
requirements.description: Inside goTo(next), .play() runs under an if (or a case) on the screen being entered: one for a win and one for a loss, or one if that asks for both. Help: 6.11.6 (Reading: Music that follows the game)
requirements.hint: if (next === 'won') { music.rate = 1.25; music.play(); }, and the same for 'lost' with rate 0.6.
